[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Password Hashing and Token Management in Flask"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Secure authentication is critical for any web application. In this tutorial, you will learn how to securely hash passwords and manage JSON Web Tokens (JWT) for user sessions in a Flask application using Werkzeug and Flask-JWT-Extended."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites and Installation"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before starting, ensure you have Python installed. You will need to install Flask and Flask-JWT-Extended. Run the following command in your terminal:"},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"pip install Flask Flask-JWT-Extended"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Setting Up Password Hashing"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Never store plaintext passwords in a database. Werkzeug provides built-in utilities using PBKDF2 with SHA256 to securely hash and verify passwords."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"from werkzeug.security import generate_password_hash, check_password_hash

password = "my_secure_password"
hashed_password = generate_password_hash(password)
print(hashed_password)

# To verify the password later:
is_valid = check_password_hash(hashed_password, "my_secure_password")
print(is_valid)  # Returns True"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Building the Flask Application"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Below is a complete Flask application that integrates password hashing for user registration and JWT creation for user login."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"from flask import Flask, jsonify, request
from flask_jwt_extended import JWTManager, create_access_token, jwt_required, get_jwt_identity
from werkzeug.security import generate_password_hash, check_password_hash

app = Flask(__name__)
app.config["JWT_SECRET_KEY"] = "super-secret-key-change-this"
jwt = JWTManager(app)

# In-memory database simulation
users = {}

@app.route("/register", methods=["POST"])
def register():
    data = request.get_json()
    username = data.get("username")
    password = data.get("password")
    
    if not username or not password:
        return jsonify({"error": "Missing username or password"}), 400
        
    if username in users:
        return jsonify({"error": "User already exists"}), 400
        
    hashed_password = generate_password_hash(password)
    users[username] = hashed_password
    
    return jsonify({"message": "User registered successfully"}), 201

@app.route("/login", methods=["POST"])
def login():
    data = request.get_json()
    username = data.get("username")
    password = data.get("password")
    
    stored_password = users.get(username)
    
    if not stored_password or not check_password_hash(stored_password, password):
        return jsonify({"error": "Invalid username or password"}), 401
        
    access_token = create_access_token(identity=username)
    return jsonify(access_token=access_token), 200

@app.route("/protected", methods=["GET"])
@jwt_required()
def protected():
    current_user = get_jwt_identity()
    return jsonify(logged_in_as=current_user), 200

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run(debug=True)"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Testing the Endpoints"},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Register a new user by sending a POST request to /register with a JSON body containing "username" and "password"."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Authenticate by sending a POST request to /login with the same credentials to receive a JWT access token."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Access the protected route at /protected by passing the token in the Authorization header as Bearer <your_token>."}]
